key_insight: This review maps bias in AI disease detection and highlights explainability, data diversity, and fairness-aware design as priorities for more equitable systems.
clinical_relevance: Bias in diagnostic AI may undermine reliability across patient populations, making subgroup evaluation and deployment oversight important.
method: Reviewed disease-detection AI studies within a stated 2015–2026 window.
Selected 23 articles from 64,389 records across seven digital libraries.
Categorized approaches by input data, model architecture, and algorithmic, demographic, model, or deployment bias.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a literature review of 23 selected articles, not a new clinical validation study, and provides no quantitative bias-reduction results.
watch_item: The review identifies research gaps but does not establish that the proposed mitigation approaches improve fairness in real-world clinical deployment.
paper_title: Fairness or Fallacy? Mapping the Landscape of AI Bias in Disease Detection
